title: Mesopelagic fish larvae off southern California did not fall in the record 2009-2023 oxygen low that a 1951-2008 oxygen relation predicted; warm-water taxa increased (CalCOFI, pre-registered test)
abstract: Question: Koslow et al. (2011) found that CalCOFI larvae of mesopelagic fishes fell in low-oxygen periods of 1951-2008 and proposed midwater oxygen as the cause. Since 2007, oxygen on sigma0 26.5 off southern California has been lower than in any 19-year window since 1950. Did the larvae stay as low as the 1951-2008 oxygen relation predicts? Approach: tests written before the 2009-2023 larval index was calculated. Annual indices of 18 mesopelagic taxa (54 core stations, January-April oblique tows; 5,346 tows in 1951-2008, 1,266 in 2009-2023), thermal groups from station temperature, oxygen and SST models fitted to 1951-2008 and tested on 2009-2023. Results: in training the index followed oxygen (r 0.54; 16 of 18 taxa positive). In 2009-2023 oxygen was 14.3 umol/kg lower, and the oxygen model predicted an index of -0.54 SD (95% interval -0.99 to -0.08); the observed mean was +0.55, and the oxygen model error was larger than that of the training mean (RMSE 1.31 vs 0.93). Cool-water taxa did not fall (+0.10 vs -0.55); warm-water taxa rose (+1.00). Across taxa, change followed SST (r 0.65, 14 of 18 signs), not oxygen (r 0.31, 7 of 18). The result held in seven pre-set sensitivities and in an identification-proof family index. Exploratory: the 60 umol/kg boundary was at its shallowest on record in 2011-2013, but larvae were above average. The 1951-2008 relation was low-frequency only (first-difference r 0.06). Limitations: larvae are not adults; one region and season; gear changes; 15 test years; 14 umol/kg is not a test of lower thresholds.
